questions.stem: In the thermite reaction, aluminium reacts with iron(III) oxide: 2Al + Fe2O3 -> Al2O3 + 2Fe. Which statement correctly identifies what is oxidised and what is reduced?

options.text: Aluminium is reduced and iron oxide is oxidised
Aluminium is oxidised and iron ions are reduced
Both aluminium and iron are oxidised
Iron oxide is reduced and aluminium oxide is oxidised

questions.explanation: Aluminium gains oxygen (forming Al2O3), so it is oxidised. Iron(III) oxide loses oxygen, so the iron ions are reduced to iron metal. In terms of electrons, Al loses electrons and Fe3+ gains electrons.

questions.stem: A student writes the half-equation: Cu2+ + 2e- -> Cu. What type of reaction does this represent?

options.text: Oxidation, because the copper is gaining electrons
Reduction, because the copper ion is losing charge
Reduction, because the copper ion is gaining electrons
Oxidation, because electrons are being transferred

questions.explanation: Reduction is the gain of electrons (remember OIL RIG: Reduction Is Gain). The Cu2+ ion gains 2 electrons to form neutral copper metal. The fact that it 'loses charge' is a consequence of gaining electrons, but the correct chemical description is that it is reduced by gaining electrons.

questions.stem: When magnesium ribbon is burned in air, it reacts with oxygen to form magnesium oxide. In terms of electron transfer, what happens to each magnesium atom?

options.text: It gains 2 electrons and is reduced
It loses 2 electrons and is oxidised
It shares 2 electrons and is neither oxidised nor reduced
It loses 1 electron and is oxidised

questions.explanation: Magnesium is in Group 2 and forms Mg2+ ions by losing 2 electrons. Losing electrons is oxidation. The half-equation is: Mg -> Mg2+ + 2e-. This is consistent with the oxygen definition too, since Mg gains oxygen.

questions.stem: In the reaction between zinc and copper sulfate solution (Zn + CuSO4 -> ZnSO4 + Cu), which species acts as the reducing agent?

options.text: Copper sulfate, because it provides the Cu2+ ions
Sulfate ions, because they remain unchanged
Copper, because it is deposited as a solid
Zinc, because it loses electrons and causes Cu2+ to be reduced

questions.explanation: The reducing agent is the substance that causes another substance to be reduced - it does this by donating electrons. Zinc is oxidised (Zn -> Zn2+ + 2e-), and the electrons it releases reduce the Cu2+ ions to Cu. The reducing agent is itself oxidised.

questions.stem: A reaction has the overall equation: 2Fe2O3 + 3C -> 4Fe + 3CO2. Which statement about this reaction is correct?

options.text: Carbon is the oxidising agent because it removes oxygen from iron oxide
This is only an oxidation reaction, not a redox reaction
Carbon is oxidised and acts as the reducing agent
Iron is oxidised because it ends up as a pure metal

questions.explanation: Carbon gains oxygen (C -> CO2), so it is oxidised. Iron oxide loses oxygen, so iron is reduced. Because carbon causes the iron to be reduced by providing electrons, carbon is the reducing agent. This is a redox reaction because both oxidation and reduction occur simultaneously.
